extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to American Sociological Review (ASR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts (articles, comments/replies) to the American Sociological Review, including formatting, anonymization, required files, ethics, and editorial criteria used to evaluate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: As editors, when we are evaluating whether or not to send a paper out for review, we have three criteria in mind—quality of methods, general sociological appeal, and breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASR papers tend to combine very strong research designs and analytic methods, general interest framing, and theory development that transcends subfields of sociology. Read recent ASR articles to see examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: General manuscript formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: All text must be double-spaced and typed in Times New Roman, 12-point font size. Margins should be at least 1 inch on all four sides. Remove any page numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All pages must be double-spaced (including notes and references) with margins measuring at least 1 inch (i.e., line length must not exceed 6-1/2 inches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: ASR Articles may not exceed 15,000 words in length including text, references, and footnotes (excluding tables and figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure word counts reported on title page; tables and figures excluded from the 15,000-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments/Replies length
rubrics_metrics.description: ASR Comments/Replies on recent publications should advance a substantive argument. Comments/Replies should not exceed 3,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload Comments and Replies directly into Sage Track; ASR does not require that Comments first be sent to article authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system and required files
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to ASR are processed electronically through Sage Track. Authors must upload an anonymous manuscript without a title page, as well as a separate title page with authors' institutional affiliations, acknowledgments, and contact information for the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will need to upload the following separate files/items into Sage Track: Cover Letter (complete contact info for corresponding author, complete manuscript title, other relevant info), Abstract (200 words or fewer describing purpose, methods, and general findings), Title Page (institutional affiliations, acknowledgments, word count, contact info), Anonymized Manuscript (no title page or self-identifying information). Pay $25 non-refundable manuscript processing fee electronically through Sage Track unless authored by ASA student members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymized manuscript / anonymous peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymized manuscripts do not include the title page (or any self identifying information). Delete or rewrite any text that identifies you as the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing your own work, write 'Smith (1992) concluded...' but do not write 'I concluded (Smith 1992)...'. To preserve anonymity, do not in general cite your own dissertations, working drafts, or unpublished papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents (separate file)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title Page: include the full article title; acknowledgments and credits; each author’s complete name and institutional affiliation(s); grant numbers and/or funding information; key words (four or five); corresponding author (name, address, phone, e-mail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title page should be uploaded separately from the anonymized manuscript so that peer review remains blind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract: upload an abstract of 200 words or fewer describing the purpose, methods, and general findings of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elsewhere the guidelines state the abstract (150 to 200 words) should not include authors' names or other identifying information. Follow 150–200 words as the expected range, and avoid identifying details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure and placeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections in a manuscript may include: (1) Title page, (2) Abstract, (3) Text, (4) Notes, (5) References, (6) Tables, (7) Figures, and (8) Appendixes. Make sure to include a placeholder for all tables and figures in the main text (e.g., insert Table 1 here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize files and placeholders so production can locate tables/figures; appendices should be lettered to distinguish from numbered tables and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and subheadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, three heading levels are sufficient to organize text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See recent issues for examples of heading use.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-text citations (author–date style) and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations in the text should provide the last name of the author(s) and year of publication. Include page numbers for direct quotes or specific passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules: (1) When author’s name is in the text, follow it with the year in parentheses—Duncan (1959). (2) When author’s name is not in the text, enclose the last name and year in parentheses—(Gouldner 1963). (3) Pages cited follow the year after a colon—(Ramirez and Weiss 1979:239–40). (4) Provide last names for joint authors—(Martin and Bailey 1988). (5) For three authors, list all three last names in the first citation—(Carr, Smith, and Jones 1962); subsequent citations use 'et al.' (6) For works with four or more authors, use 'et al.' throughout. (7) For institutional authorship, supply minimal identification from the complete citation—(U.S. Bureau of the Census 1963:117). (8) List a series of citations in alphabetical order or date order separated by semicolons—(Burgess 1968; Marwell et al. 1971). (9) Use 'forthcoming' to cite sources scheduled for publication. (10) For machine-readable data files, cite authorship and date. (11) To preserve anonymity, do not in general cite your own dissertations, working drafts, or unpublished papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes formatting and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes should be numbered in the text consecutively using superscript Arabic numerals. Notes should be typed, double-spaced, in a separate 'NOTES' section. Begin each note with the superscript numeral to which it is keyed in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes can (a) explain or amplify text, (b) cite materials of limited availability, or (c) append information presented in a table or figure. Avoid long notes: consider alternatives (state info is available from the author, deposit info in a national retrieval center, or add an appendix). Each note should not exceed 100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: References section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: References are presented in a separate section headed 'REFERENCES.' All references cited in the text must be listed in the reference section, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication information must be complete and correct. List references in alphabetical order by authors’ last names; include first names and middle initials for all authors when available. List two or more entries by the same author(s) in order of the year of publication. When cited material is accepted for publication, use 'Forthcoming' in place of the date and give the journal name or publishing house. For dissertations and unpublished papers, cite the date and place presented and/or where available; if no date use 'n.d.' If two or more cited works are by the same author(s) within the same year, list them in alphabetical order by title and distinguish by adding letters a, b, c to the year (or to 'Forthcoming'). For works with more than one author, only invert the name of the first author (e.g., 'Jones, Arthur B., Colin D. Smith, and James Petersen'). List all authors; using 'et al.' in the reference list is not acceptable. References for data sets should include a persistent identifier (DOI). Refer to the ASA Style Guide (7th ed., 2022) for additional examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting examples and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide correct formats/examples for Books, Periodicals, Collections, Dissertations, Web sites, Datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow provided examples (e.g., Bernard [1865] 1957. An Introduction..., Goodman 1947a and 1947b examples, Sampson 1992 in edited volume, dissertation citation format, dataset citation with ICPSR identifier and DOI example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: numbering and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered consecutively in the order in which they appear in the text and must include table titles. Each table must include a descriptive title and headings for all columns and rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables will appear in the published article in the order in which they are numbered initially. Gather general notes to tables as 'Note:'; use a, b, c, etc., for table footnotes. Use asterisks *, **, and *** to indicate significance at the p < .05, p < .01, and p < .001 levels, respectively, and always specify one-tailed or two-tailed tests. Generally, results at p > .05 (such as p < .10) should not be indicated as significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: numbering, captions, and preferred formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered consecutively in the order in which they appear in the text and must include figure captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures will appear in the published article in the order in which they are numbered initially. Preferred programs and formats for figures include: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, .wmf, .emf, and .tiff (300 dpi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placeholders for tables and figures in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure to include a placeholder for all tables and figures in the main text (e.g., insert Table 1 here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reviewers/readers and production find the intended location for tables/figures during review and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Use consecutive Arabic numerals in parentheses at the right margin to identify important equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number equations consecutively for reference in text and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendixes labeling and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendixes should be lettered to distinguish them from numbered tables and figures. Include a descriptive title for each appendix (e.g., 'Appendix A. Variable Names and Definitions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices are separate from the NOTES and REFERENCES sections and should be clearly labeled and titled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for copyrighted material
rubrics_metrics.description: The author(s) are responsible for securing permission to reproduce all copyrighted figures or materials before they are published by ASR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the written permission must be included with the manuscript submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should familiarize themselves with Sage’s Accessibility Guidelines to ensure their manuscripts meet recognized accessibility standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Sage’s guidance on making materials accessible (e.g., for figures, tables, alternative text) as part of submission preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID collection and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of ORCID iDs from corresponding authors is now part of the submission process of this journal. Corresponding authors will be asked to associate their ORCID iD to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASR encourages all co-authors to link their ORCID ID to their accounts in the online peer review platforms. ORCID iDs become part of accepted publication metadata and are published with the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: simultaneous submission, prior publication, and plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript to another professional journal while it is under review by the ASR is regarded by the ASA as unethical. Significant findings or contributions that have already appeared (or will appear) elsewhere must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All persons who publish in ASA journals are required to abide by ASA guidelines and ethics codes regarding plagiarism and other ethical issues. Disclose prior or concurrent publication and adhere to ASA policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-sharing policy expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: ASA’s stated policy on data-sharing: 'As a regular practice, sociologists share data and pertinent documentation as an integral part of a research plan.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sociologists generally make their data available after completion of a project or its major publications, except where proprietary agreements or confidentiality (e.g., field notes, ethnographic interview details) preclude sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage has introduced a policy to enable name and pronoun changes for our authors. ASA journals published by Sage follow this policy. All requests to make a name or pronoun change will be honored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes name changes because of marriage, divorce, gender affirmation, religious conversion, etc.; more information available via Sage’s Name Change Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript processing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: $25.00 Non-refundable Manuscript Processing Fee. Authors must pay the non-refundable $25.00 manuscript processing fee electronically through Sage Track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All new manuscripts require a fee unless authored by ASA student members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on resubmission of previously rejected ASR papers
rubrics_metrics.description: ASR does not consider submissions of papers previously rejected at the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not resubmit a paper that was previously rejected by ASR without addressing journal policy or substantial revision as per guidance (note: guideline is explicit 'does not consider').
